description: Mystery manual automation fire 2026-09-18 14:16:29 UTC: a conductor run appeared although the schedule trigger was breaker-disabled and nobody clicked Run now. Root cause: a LEFT-RUNNING /iterate sibling session with a 10-minute rlm heartbeat (Line-watch ceremony) fires the automation through its ALWAYS-ENABLED api trigger (trigger_id manual) using the user fabro CLI token whenever the line stalls. Disabling the schedule cron does NOT stop it. Forensics that identified it: (1) traefik JSON access log on the docker host - grep POST /api/v1/automations, shows ClientHost + /auth/cli/refresh signature; (2) ~/.fabro/logs/cli.<date>.log shows repeated fabro events calls on the current run; (3) agent_observe.list_agents() reveals a running sibling; its session jsonl contains heartbeat_prompt entries. Also: a dying watcher session wrote tracker claims that were overstated (c42f closed as validated-live although the smoke pass exited Already-landed; PR #237 called published although still draft) - verify runtime premises of agent-written closures before trusting them.
resolution: User terminated the sibling session + its heartbeat (2026-09-18 ~15:00 UTC); both schedule triggers manually stopped for the calm window; conductor stays off until the full-cycle smoke decision. Guard: when deliberately stopping the line, also check for line-watch heartbeats/sessions - scheduler-off does not mean nothing will fire.

name: stranded-run-salvage-via-checkpoint-branch
description: Salvage pattern for stranded runs (2026-09-15, run 01M2J1BA2J): a terminal-failed run carries its full work in the committed checkpoint branch (origin/fabro/run/<id>, sha = final_git_commit_sha from run.failed). Salvage = fetch the branch, cherry-pick the implementer commit onto current denkhaus, adapt to whatever landed in between (here: v0.356 billing->usage rename; compiler E0559/E0425 lists every fixture site), then fork-pin per policy BEFORE merging so the next upstream merge cannot drop the feature. Verify the cherry-pick compiles immediately: textual auto-merge success says nothing about type renames.
